text:
maria: Heads-up — planning a terraform apply for `release-2026.03` today in the 18:00 UTC change window. Targets: VPC route updates + cross-account IAM trust. Requesting runbook sanity check and rollback plan.

alex: Are we going to route this through deploybot or run manual applies? We've got a couple of queued merges in the merge lane.

deploybot: [automated] Deploybot check: 3 queued infra merges (PR #412, #419, #421). No lock on tfstate detected. Recommend draining merge lane until apply window.

chris: +1 to drain. Also recommend serial applies for the IAM pieces (one account at a time) to avoid cross-account race conditions.

samir: Quick check — are we pinning provider versions? Last time provider drift caused plan diffs. Suggest pinning aws provider to `~> 4.12.1` for this release.

maria: Good call. I'll add provider pin in the release branch. Also planning a small preflight: `terraform plan -var 'release=2026.03' -out=release-2026-03.plan` and export the plan artifact to the release notes.

alex: For tfstate locking: if the deploybot shows a stale lock we should use `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>` only after verifying there are no running applies. Oncall-bot, can you block new merges 15m before the window?

oncall-bot: [automated] Merge queue freeze scheduled at 17:45 UTC. Notifications will be sent to PR authors.

maria: Runbook outline (short):
1) freeze merges @17:45 UTC
2) preflight plan uploaded by 17:50 UTC
3) deploybot serial apply sequence starts 18:00 UTC (VPC, then IAM-account-A, then IAM-account-B)
4) smoke tests (connectivity + cross-account assume-role) 18:15-18:25 UTC
5) if failed, rollback via tagged state & apply previous plan (see commands below)

chris: Commands for rollback we discussed:
```
# assume we have rollback.tfvars pointing to previous module versions
terraform apply -var-file=rollback.tfvars release-2026-03.plan
# or if we need to force previous state snapshot
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-tfstate/backups/tfstate-2026-03-previous.tfstate ./terraform.tfstate
terraform init && terraform apply -auto-approve
```

samir: Also capture exact plan id + SHA in release notes so we can re-apply the same plan if needed. That prevents drift causing different outcomes.

alex: One more: deploybot should emit a safety flag if the plan contains >50 route changes or >10 IAM role updates. We should fail fast and escalate.

deploybot: [automated] Preflight scan: plan size = 12 route changes, 3 IAM updates — OK. No safety flag.

maria: Okay let's proceed with that. I'll update the release branch with provider pin, add the plan artifact, and tag the plan SHA in the release notes. Setting a canary hold: deploybot will apply VPC only first and wait for :thumbsup: from @alex and @chris before continuing.

alex: I'll be on watch. If the VPC apply shows more than 200ms median latency change across edge routers, we stop and roll back.

oncall-bot: [automated] Reminder scheduled at 17:50 UTC: upload preflight plan.

maria: Thanks all — final checklists: add runbook snippet to the PR description, verify KMS keys for cross-account apply are accessible, and ensure support has the rollback artifact. Will post plan artifact link when uploaded. :raised_hands:

chris: If anything funky happens ping me directly. I'll be online until 19:30 UTC.

maria: Plan uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/release-2026-03/plan-abc123 (attached to PR). Deploybot hold is set to 'canary-wait'.

deploybot: [automated] Hold set: canary-wait. VPC apply scheduled at 18:00 UTC.

alex: Acknowledged. Monitoring config: 
- logs -> cloudwatch/infrastructure/changes
- trace -> xray:infra-changes
- smoke tests -> infra/smoke/release-2026-03-runner
I'll report 2 min after VPC apply completes.

maria: Perfect. Closing for now — will reopen thread if preflight shows drift or errors.
